catalog_quote: 1.1.2. Prosodie. Dans cette section, nous nous intéressons aux éléments phoniques (autres que les phonèmes) qui ont une fonction distinctive: le ton, l’accent, l’intonation et le rythme La langue mbochi ne possède pas de structuration accentuelle ou rythmique qui puisse déterminer des groupements de la taille du Groupe. (Aborobongui 2011 :11, Rialland et al. 2009, Embanga et al. 2011). Aussi allons-nous parler des tons et des syllabes. [...] 1.1.2.2. Tonologie. Dans cette section, nous parlons des tonèmes du parler mbochi olee. Comme bien d’autres langues de son groupe, le mbochi est une langue à tons. C'est-à-dire, on peut y opposer des mots par ailleurs identiques mais se distinguant par la variation de la hauteur mélodique.

new_statements.translation: 1.1.2. Prosody. In this section we consider the phonic elements (other than phonemes) that have a distinctive function: tone, accent/stress, intonation and rhythm. The Mbochi language has no accentual or rhythmic structuring that could determine groupings of the size of the [phonological] Group (Aborobongui 2011:11, Rialland et al. 2009, Embanga et al. 2011). We shall therefore speak of tones and syllables. [...] [p.70] Like many other languages of its group, Mbochi is a tone language; that is, words otherwise identical can be opposed solely by a difference in pitch.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbochi is described as a two-tone language (H vs L, TBU = mora/syllable, lexical and grammatical tone) with no accentual (stress) or rhythmic organisation; the author explicitly sets accent and rhythm aside as non-existent in the language and treats only tone and syllable structure as distinctive prosodic units. No stress position is posited anywhere in the 555-page description of the ten dialects.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The statement is made for 'la langue mbochi' generally within the chapter on the Olee (Boundji) reference dialect; the dialect-comparison chapters discuss only segmental and tonal variation.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns word/phrase prosody generally: absence of accentual structure is invoked to explain why prosodic grouping (Groupe Phonologique / Groupe Intonatif, after Rialland & Aborobongui) is defined by hiatus resolution, tone processes and boundary tones rather than by stress. It is a brief assertion resting on cited conference work by Rialland & Embanga Aborobongui rather than on the author's own argumentation, though the author is a native-speaker linguist describing his own field data.
new_statements.identity_note: Kouarata's phonology chapter (Part II ch.1 sec.1.1) is headed 'Analyse phonologique du parler Olee' (the Boundji/Olee variety, his reference dialect, C25B in his internal numbering), but the deciding sentence is phrased for 'la langue mbochi' as a whole and the thesis covers all ten dialects (Olee, Mbondzi, Tsambitso, Ngilima, Bokwele, Bonyala, Ngae, Obaa, Eboyi, Ondinga). Aborobongui 2013 describes the Mbondzi variety; Bedrosian 1996/97 and Fontaney 1988 describe Boundji/Olee. All fall under mbos1242 (ISO mdw).

tone_statements.quote: Mboshi is a two tone Bantu language whose words are typically composed of roots and affixes. ... With respect to tones, the high tone is coded using an acute accent on the vowel while low tone vowel has no special marker. Word root, prefix and suffix all bear specific tones which tend to be realized as such in their surface forms. ... In our transcriptions, Mboshi’s tonal system consisting of a pair of high and low tones is simply represented using diacritics on vowels ... The distinction between high and low tones is phonological (see [14]).
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.1 pp. 2-3 and sec. 2.2 p. 3 with footnote 3
tone_statements.summary: NLP paper; two-tone (H/L) sketch credited to Rialland & Aborobongui 2016 [14]; says each of 7 vowels may carry H or L, affixes bear own tones, tones mark tense; no stress remark.

tone_statements.citation: Rialland, Annie & Martial Embanga Aborobongui. 2016. How intonations interact with tones in Embosi (Bantu C25), a two-tone language without downdrift. In Laura J. Downing & Annie Rialland (eds.), Intonation in African Tone Languages (Phonology and Phonetics 24), 195-222. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
tone_statements.quote: Embosi is a two-tone language whose tone-bearing unit is the mora. There is no word or root level tonal patterns like the ones found in neighboring languages such as Kukuya ... Thus, any type of tone combination can be found on mono, bi or tri-moraic nominal roots ... given that Embosi does not allow tonal contours on a single mora or downstep. ... The fact that the L tone is active in the tonal process indicates that the contrast between H and L tones in Embosi is a binary one and not a privative one.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2 'Basic features of Embosi tonology', pp. 196-198
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H and L on the mora; no word melodies, no tone shift/spread, no contour on one mora, no downstep and no downdrift (F0 study, 2 speakers); metatony on verbs; focus has no prominence.

tone_statements.citation: Embanga Aborobongui, Georges Martial, Fatima Hamlaoui & Annie Rialland. 2014. Syntactic and prosodic aspects of left and right dislocation in Embɔsi (Bantu C25). ZAS Papers in Linguistics 57 (Proceedings of the Workshop BantuSynPhonIS: preverbal domain(s)): 26-48.
tone_statements.quote: As many Bantu languages, Embɔsi is a two tone language. The tone bearing unit is the mora, or the syllable if long vowels are analyzed as sequences of two identical short vowels. ... One of the striking characteristics of Embɔsi is the fact that it does not have downstep or downdrift. ... In Embɔsi, an assertive sentence can be uttered on two tone levels (one for the H tone and the second one for the L tone) until it reaches the ending part, which is lowered due to the final assertive intonation.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 34-35, sec. 4.1.1 'A two-tone language without downdrift'
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H/L, mora as TBU, no downstep/downdrift; L not a default tone; boundary tones L%/H% superimposed; verbal metatony. F0 figures.

tone_statements.quote: Par ailleurs, le mbochi possède deux tons : un ton haut et un ton bas. Chaque ton est porté par une more et toute more porte un ton. Une contrainte absolue interdit tout contour sur une more et déclenche des processus permettant d’éviter toute configuration non conforme, en particulier, à la suite de l’élision de voyelle (voir Embanga Aborobongui et al., sous presse).
tone_statements.translation: Moreover, Mbochi has two tones: a high tone and a low tone. Each tone is borne by a mora and every mora bears a tone. An absolute constraint forbids any contour on a mora and triggers processes that avoid any non-conforming configuration, in particular following vowel elision (see Embanga Aborobongui et al., in press).
tone_statements.locator: p. 4, sec. 2.3 'Principales caractéristiques phonologiques du mbochi'
tone_statements.summary: Two tones H/L, mora as TBU, contours banned on a mora; tonal restructuring after elision referred to Embanga Aborobongui et al. (in press). Tones not coded in the ASR lexicon (p. 7).

tone.quote: Embosi is a two-tone language whose tone-bearing unit is the mora. There is no word or root level tonal patterns like the ones found in neighboring languages such as Kukuya ... Thus, any type of tone combination can be found on mono, bi or tri-moraic nominal roots ... given that Embosi does not allow tonal contours on a single mora or downstep. ... The fact that the L tone is active in the tonal process indicates that the contrast between H and L tones in Embosi is a binary one and not a privative one.
tone.locator: sec. 2 'Basic features of Embosi tonology', pp. 196-198
tone.summary: Two level tones H and L on the mora; no word melodies, no tone shift/spread, no contour on one mora, no downstep and no downdrift (F0 study, 2 speakers); metatony on verbs; focus has no prominence.
